newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends down as rates seen falling.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends down as rates seen falling.

text.p: * Low inflation seen pushing interest rates down
The Philippine peso ended lower as Friday's news of a lower than expected inflation rate in September strengthened belief that rates would fall at the next treasury bills auction, traders said.
The peso closed at 26.268 to the dollar versus Thursday's close of 26.26. The weighted average was 26.264 against the previous 26.257.
September's inflation rate at 4.4 percent turned out lower than the market had expected. It was 7.9 percent in August.
"Sentiment is still more of continuous fall of the peso," one trader said, adding the Central Bank was limiting the fall.
"I see a downside at the T-bill auction on Monday," he said.
Traders said demand from some foreign funds who were taking profits on their equities portfolio might have also put pressure on the peso.
Volume was $123.25 million versus the previous $114 million.
